summary: Mt. Hood NF lookout: 1920s wooden tower, 1949 L-4 replacement, destroyed in the October 1962 Columbus Day storm; Oregon Hikers says only the foundation remains.

facts.design: 40-foot wooden tower with 7x7 cab and ground cabin (1920s); 41-foot treated-timber L-4 tower (1949)
facts.status_note: Tower destroyed in the October 1962 Columbus Day storm and not rebuilt; cabin burned in the 1970s; Oregon Hikers says only the foundation remains
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Mt. Hood National Forest)

access.note: Sources describe a popular hike to the summit; the lake area is reached past an entry booth on Road 13 (SummitPost). No closure reported.

visit.trail_note: About 2.3 miles on foot from Lost Lake Trailhead (Oregon Hikers); SummitPost gives 1.9 miles and 1,330 feet of climb from the lake shore.

events.note: Original 40-foot wooden tower with 7x7 cab and ground cabin; sources give only the 1920s, so 1920 is a decade placeholder
41-foot treated-timber L-4 tower (register, firelookout.com); a district history quoted on Weebly dates the contract build to February 7, 1950
Lookout lost its roof to high winds in October, per a district history quoted under a February 9, 1959 entry
Closed except as an emergency lookout (district history, February 9, 1959 entry)
Tower destroyed in the Columbus Day storm of October 12, 1962; not rebuilt
1963 annual report says the tower was salvaged and its material and hardware were intended for Postage Stamp Lookout; this does not match the destroyed account
Original log cabin burned in the 1970s; sources give only the decade, so 1970 is a decade placeholder
Registered August 26, 2010 with Former Fire Lookout Sites

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com date the 41-foot replacement to 1949. A district history quoted on Weebly is dated February 7, 1950 for the contract build. Not resolved; the story gives both.

The register and firelookout.com say the tower was destroyed in 1962. A 1963 annual report quoted on Weebly says the tower was salvaged, with material meant for Postage Stamp Lookout. Not resolved; the record keeps destroyed in 1962 and the story flags the salvage note.

The register and firelookout.com call the October 1962 storm a hurricane. Willamette Heritage Center says it was an extra tropical cyclone. The story uses the storm's date and name and notes the difference.

notes_for_editor: Four sources agree on the 1920s tower, the 1962 storm loss and the burned cabin. They disagree on the replacement year (1949 vs a February 1950 contract date) and on whether the tower was destroyed or salvaged (1963 report). Today's condition rests on one hike guide (Oregon Hikers: only the foundation remains); no Forest Service source was read. The 1920 and 1970 event years are decade placeholders. height_m 12.5 is the 41-foot 1949 tower converted to metres. Access is public per the hike guides, with no closure found.
